findings.claim: 'Windows Job Object' kill has no build path. Node has no Job Object API, so it needs a native addon (against no-npm, no-native-binding ADR-0002) or a helper exe. Doc does not say which. v1 uses taskkill /F /T.
findings.evidence: PRD-v2.md:138 'Kill: Unix process group; Windows Job Object.' TECH-SPEC §8 same. v1 src/executor.ts:196-206 killTree uses execSync('taskkill /F /T /PID ...'); executor.ts:445 detached: !isWin.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY 8a778ba9 2026-03-01 'fix: Windows process tree kill (taskkill /F /T) + fix recursive killTree'. ORIGINAL_INTENT: 'shell: true spawns cmd.exe which doesn't die with SIGKILL alone ... fixes the Windows CI hanging on timeout tests'. REGRESSION_RISK: if Job Object is not buildable, a late swap to child.kill() re-opens CI hangs and orphans. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: tree kill must reach grandchildren of bash.exe/cmd.exe; no native addon.
findings.fix: State the mechanism: taskkill /F /T /PID (v1, proven) or name the helper. Add a GP4 Windows case: bash spawns a grandchild sleep; after timeout/cancel no process of the tree is alive.

findings.claim: G7 + §8 'Runtimes found by PATH lookup' do not say how Git Bash is found. Plain PATH lookup of bash on Windows hits WSL C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe or WindowsApps first, or the Git\cmd shim. v1 fixed both.
findings.evidence: PRD-v2.md:137 'Runtimes found by PATH lookup'; :192 'Windows language:"shell" = Git Bash; missing -> hard error'. v1 src/runtime.ts:174-222 skips 'system32'/'windowsapps' and canonicalizes to Git\usr\bin\bash.exe.
findings.archaeology: 02cd08e6 2026-03-03 'fix(windows): detect Git Bash via known paths, not PATH lookup': 'MCP server processes often inherit a minimal PATH that includes Git\cmd but not Git\usr\bin'. e2bce0b5 2026-06-13 'preserve Git Bash path conversion for native git (#826)'. 6b6193e7 2026-06-21 (#796) gates on `where bash` but keeps the WSL skip and the canonical path. REGRESSION_RISK: WSL bash gets Windows paths and fails; Git\cmd shim loses MSYS path conversion for native git (#826). SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: skip System32/WindowsApps; prefer Git\usr\bin\bash.exe; no fallback to pwsh/cmd (owner rule) -> hard error with the found candidates named.
findings.fix: Add to TECH-SPEC §8 the exact Windows bash resolution rule (exclusions + canonical path) and a GP4 Windows test where WSL bash is first on PATH.

GP4', :211 '791', :221 '826'. v2-issue-map.md:384 '1154 Windows: windowsHide on probes ... B'. v1 executor.ts:446-450 windowsHide comment 'leaving the MCP response empty'.

findings.claim: E12 says hook command is `node "<launcher>" hook ...` and works in PowerShell. E15 says the launcher writes an absolute node path. A command that starts with a quoted absolute path is a string in PowerShell and fails without `&` (#993). v1 builds exactly that shape.
findings.evidence: PRD-v2.md:166 E12; :169 E15 'Launcher writes the PATH-resolved, non-versioned node path'. v1 src/adapters/types.ts:430 return `"${runtimePath}" "${safePath}"`. Snapshot tickets/data/isall.json #993 OPEN '[Bug]: Windows hook commands fail under PowerShell (missing call operator `&`)'.
findings.archaeology: v1 shape from buildHookRuntimeCommand (types.ts:418); claude-code/hooks.ts:161 comment 'Uses process.execPath + forward slashes to avoid PATH issues and MSYS path mangling on Windows (#369, #372)'. REGRESSION_RISK: bare `node` re-opens #369 (PATH) ; quoted path keeps #993. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: one command string must run in cmd, PowerShell and bash; paths with spaces; forward slashes.
findings.fix: Pick one shape and state it per host shell, e.g. unquoted `node` when the host runs hooks via PowerShell, or a host-specific `&` prefix from adapters/table.ts. GP3 runs the generated command in cmd, powershell, pwsh and Git Bash with a node path that has a space.

findings.claim: Report has only 'os' for Windows. Most v1 Windows bugs depend on shell and path facts the report cannot show. Owner rule: issue form must make the agent send maximum debug data.
findings.evidence: ADR-0014:30 'os, node + node:sqlite + fts5'; :32 'path facts (has_space, non_ascii, max_len)'. Windows classes: #993 (host hook shell), #372 'Windows + Git Bash when cwd is on non-C: drive (MSYS' (test-ledger:69), #826 bash kind, #548 space.
findings.fix: Add enum rows (no path text, passes the typed scanner): win_bash: gitbash_usr|gitbash_cmd|wsl|msys2|none; hook_shell: cmd|powershell|pwsh|bash|unknown; pwsh_present: bool; drive_is_c: bool; path_has_backslash_mix: bool; long_paths_enabled: bool; last_kill: taskkill_ok|tree_alive|none.

findings.claim: DB key `<git-common-dir-hash>` is not normalized. On Windows, Git Bash git prints /c/Users/..., native git prints C:/Users/..., hosts send c:\users\.... Same repo gives different hashes and split DBs.
findings.evidence: ADR-0002:23 '~/.context-mode/projects/<git-common-dir-hash>/context.db'. No normalization rule in ADR-0002 or TECH-SPEC (grep 'normaliz' finds none for this).
findings.archaeology: Unverified in v1 for this exact key; v1 had per-agent dirs (ADR-0002:7).
findings.fix: Define the hash input: realpath, Windows drive letter upper-case, backslash to '/', MSYS /c/ form to C:/, case-fold on win32. GP7 case: same repo opened from Git Bash and PowerShell gives one DB.

findings.claim: 'Containment: path checks by path components' does not cover Windows: case-insensitive compare, drive letters, UNC, \\?\ prefix, '/' vs '\\'.
findings.evidence: PRD-v2.md:142 'Containment: path checks by path components, not string prefix (#1294)'.
findings.fix: State: compare path.win32 components after resolve, case-folded, drive and UNC root must match; add GP7 Windows cases.

findings.claim: 'switch to it atomically (rename)' of a version dir fails on Windows with EPERM/EBUSY while any process has a file open or cwd inside it. Also no CLI exists (G12-G14), so who runs this is unclear.
findings.evidence: ADR-0010:46 'switch to it atomically (rename)'. v1 26d346d2 2026-03-02 'Merge pull request #31 from mksglu/fix/windows-ebusy-cleanup: fix: handle EBUSY on Windows temp dir cleanup'.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY 26d346d2 (PR #31) - Windows EBUSY on dir removal. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: never rename/delete a dir a running server or hook uses.
findings.fix: Use a pointer file (current -> version dir) written via temp+rename of the file, and delete old dirs only when unused; add a Windows GP11 case with the server running.
